A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Self-REF. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including material relocated between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing, rejection, calibration, gradient-masking and transfer experiments, plus model-response case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the transfer experiment now presented in Section 5.5.

M1.justification: Confidence-token annotation, token initialization, masking of incorrect-answer gradients, fine-tuning and normalized confidence extraction remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the routing/rejection procedures are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use MMLU, OpenbookQA, GSM8K and MedQA with the same routing and rejection tasks. OpenbookQA-to-MMLU transfer already appeared in v1 Appendix D; its placement in v2 Section 5.5 adds no coverage.

E2.justification: The four confidence baselines and the random-routing comparator retain their participation in corresponding experiments. Zero-shot Logits receives a different citation, but its described procedure and reported comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The models, LoRA ranks, training budgets, sample counts, prompts, metrics and routing thresholds match. Both versions remove the correct choice from 50% of rejection examples and retain the same transfer protocol.

E4.justification: The gradient-masking ablation, calibration-versus-utility analysis, transfer experiment and case studies are retained. Moving transfer from Appendix D to Section 5.5 does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose the same fixed inference seed, 2024. Neither reports additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted curves and case-study responses match. Examples include the 39% Llama3-8B MMLU routing rate and the transfer routing rates of 75% for Mistral and 70% for Llama3; the latter results are relocated.

T1.justification: The dataset notation, augmented-data definitions, confidence formula and threshold rules are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about confidence tokens and their routing/rejection benefits. Wording changes do not expand the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 add the rationale that consistency across resampled answers can diverge from correctness, explaining Self-REF's correctness-based confidence target. Routing and transfer interpretations remain; the latency/privacy caveats repeated in Section 6 already existed in v1 Appendix A.

D1.justification: Baseline prompts, hyperparameters, adapter placement, decoding instructions, training times and hardware disclosures are unchanged. v1 Appendix E becomes v2 Appendix D without new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 expand positioning against resampling-based uncertainty and LLM cascades. Six references are added, including SelfCheckGPT, the [idk]-token paper and EcoAssistant; Duan et al. is removed, and Zero-shot Logits is instead attributed to Mahaut et al.

P1.justification: v2 adds 'LLMs' to the title, edits prose and contribution formatting, promotes the transfer appendix to Section 5.5 and repeats existing limitations in Section 6. Rewriting is localized, mainly in related work, with most text retained.

P2.justification: Figure 5 moves into the main text, Figure 4 is enlarged and repositioned with a revised caption, and other figures receive small placement or sizing adjustments. All seven figures and six tables remain, with unchanged underlying results.

improvement.justification: The expanded related-work discussion better explains the intended distinction from consistency-based uncertainty and external routing models. Bringing existing transfer evidence and cost/privacy caveats into the main narrative improves accessibility. These are limited gains: scientific evidence is unchanged, caveats are duplicated, and Section 6 contains the malformed reference 'Appendix 5.5'.
